title: Cheat curls tutorial (theoretical aspects)
summary: NH explains that he built most of his biceps with cheat curls, which he did daily for his first three years without knowing the difference from strict curls. He doesn't recommend them but defends their logic: they bypass the weak bottom range where leverage is poor, and they spare the biceps during the riskiest phase.
claims: He has done cheat curls every week for seven years and gained most of his biceps size from them
For his first five years the only biceps work he did was cheat curls; he never curled strictly because he did not know there was a difference
For his first three years he cheat-curled every single day, effectively a high-intensity, high-frequency, low-volume nucleus overload, and his biceps remain one of his best body parts
He does not promote cheat curls; it was probably not the smartest approach and he was lucky never to get injured
Biceps injuries almost never happen on the positive; they happen at the end of the negative or the switch to the positive, when force hits an overloaded, overextended tendon
With proper cheat curls, the riskiest part of the range for the biceps is moved by the whole body, not the biceps

Cheat curl injuries come from improper form, like curling too early and dumping kinetic energy into an extended biceps; that is no more the lift's fault than lower back injury from rounding in a squat
Many people are dogmatic about cheating, and even once they accept it they try to standardize it; a partial is also a form of cheating
His cheat curls help the start of the positive; the gains come from the end of the positive and he ignores the negative
In a perfect world everyone would grow with strict form, because it controls failure and progression best and has the lowest injury risk
You don't need cheat curls for bigger biceps; curls in general are all you need
Cheat curls take out the bottom of the curl, where leverage is poor and the front delt does much of the work (a source of EZ-bar injuries); the biceps works mainly past 45 degrees
The point of cheat reps is to get a muscle into the range where it is stronger so it can be overloaded; cheat rows initiated with the legs follow the same logic
If you are emotionally attached to a lift and it serves you well, keep it even if it breaks conventional hypertrophy rules
He is currently only maintaining biceps size with a medium-frequency, high-intensity approach, and cheat curls let him accumulate tonnage quickly with no injury risk
Always try new things, starting light, to see how your body responds
exercises: use the body to get past the bottom range, finish the top half with the biceps; do not curl too early
bypasses the low-leverage bottom range to overload the strong range
initiate with leg drive, finish the pull, stretch back
gets past the weakest bottom portion to overload the upper back
